## Pre-registration

The analysis plan was committed and tagged `analysis-plan-v1` before any treatment-effect
estimate existed. An amendment (`analysis-plan-v1.1`), also made before any estimate, added a
pre-period-detrended secondary specification for every design. Every later change is in the
[deviations log](https://github.com/Gnanasudharsan/nyc-congestion-pricing-causal-impact/blob/main/docs/deviations.md).
Each entry is dated and says whether it was made before or after the related estimate was
seen.

- [Analysis plan](https://github.com/Gnanasudharsan/nyc-congestion-pricing-causal-impact/blob/main/docs/analysis-plan.md)
- [Architecture decision records (ADRs 0001–0012)](https://github.com/Gnanasudharsan/nyc-congestion-pricing-causal-impact/tree/main/docs/adr)

## Designs

| Design | Used for | Key choices |
|---|---|---|
| DiD / event study | Facility, taxi-zone, station, route, and site panels | Unit × season and date fixed effects; anticipation window as its own term; 2023 as the event-study seasonal baseline (ADR 0012) |
| Detrended DiD | Every DiD (amendment 1) | Unit trends fitted on the pre-period only, then extrapolated |
| Synthetic control | Systems (NTD) and monitors | Demeaned; non-negative weights summing to 1, solved exactly by NNLS; placebo-in-space RMSPE-ratio inference |
| Stacked heterogeneity | Peak/overnight, weekday/weekend, vehicle class, borough | Level-specific fixed effects; SEs for differences clustered by the original unit |
| Zone effects | Equity lens (exploratory) | Placebo-in-time noise; DerSimonian–Laird empirical Bayes |

## Inference

- **30 or more clusters:** cluster-robust standard errors with t(G − 1) critical values. These
  match `pyfixest` exactly on every unadjusted design.
- **Fewer than 30 clusters:**
  - restricted wild cluster bootstrap-t with Webb weights. The estimators are linear in the
    outcome, so each replication re-estimates the pre-period adjustment exactly;
  - randomization inference over every assignment of treated status.
- **Multiplicity:** Holm across the six primary outcomes; Benjamini–Hochberg within each
  secondary family.
- **Parallel-trends sensitivity:** HonestDiD relative-magnitudes and smoothness bounds
  [@rambachan2023]. The Python port was validated against the R package's published example
  (20 of 20 interval endpoints to two decimals). It runs in its own locked environment because
  it requires NumPy 1.x.

## Testing on simulated data

Every estimator is unit-tested on simulated panels with known effects. The tests cover:

- recovery of pooled and event-study effects;
- removal of a pre-existing trend by detrending;
- removal of weather confounding by the weather adjustment;
- the bootstrap and randomization-inference p-values;
- synthetic-control weights.

The simulations caught one flaw in the plan as written: the seasonal collinearity in the
event study described in ADR 0012.
